tasks.title: Star rise in Moletai
tasks.statement: An observer in Moletai recorded that a star culminated at 02:54 and set at 05:45 on September 8, 2013. Effects of irregularities of the horizon should not be taken into account.

parts.question: At what time will the star rise on September 9, 2013?
parts.reference:
The time elapsed from the rising of the star to culmination is equal to the time elapsed from culmination to set. Therefore, on September 8, this star rose at 02:54 — 02:51 = 0:03. The next time the star will rise after a sidereal day, equal to 23:56, that is, at 23:59 but still on September 8. On September 9 the star will rise after one more sidereal day, that is at 23:55.

Критерии оценивания (Всего 5 пт):
- Understanding approach that culmination is the middle point between star rise and star set — 1 pt.
- Time of the first star rise on September 8 calculation, result 0:03 — 1 pt.
- Using sidereal approach for the future calculations — 1 pt.
- Issue that next sunrise will be still on September 8 — 1 pt.
- On September 9 the star will rise after one more sidereal day, that is at 23:55 — 1 pt.

parts.question: In approximately which direction do you need to wait for the rising of the star? Choose one of the alternatives: N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW. Draw a picture with an explanation.
parts.reference:
Very roughly one can say that the star is above the horizon 3/4 days, and under the horizon — 1/4 days. The star culminates at south. Accordingly, it is above the horizon: 3/8 of rotation before the culmination and 3/8 of rotation after, that is, it rises approximately at south-east and sets approximately at south-west. Answer: SE.

Критерии оценивания (Всего 3 пт):
- Argumentation about the star is above the horizon 3/4 days, 3/8 of rotation before the culmination and 3/8 of rotation after — 1 pt.
- Correct illustration — 1 pt.
- Rises approximately at south-east, answer: SE — 1 pt.

tasks.title: Gliese 581 g
tasks.statement: This celestial body in the system of the star Gliese 581 is the most Earth-like planet found outside the Solar System, and the exoplanet with the greatest recognized potential for harboring albuminous based life.

parts.question: Estimate orbital period t of Gliese 581 g. Consider the orbit to be circular.
parts.reference:
In the 'data of some stars' table one can find the mass of the star Gliese 581, which is equal to Meg = 0.31 Mo, its parallax p = 0.16", and the apparent bolometric magnitude m = 8.0. Knowing the parallax and the apparent bolometric magnitude of the star, one can find its absolute bolometric magnitude: M = m + 5 + 5 lg p = 8.0 + 5 + (-3.98) = 9.0. It is 9.0 - 4.8 = 4.2 greater than the absolute magnitude of the Sun. Thus, the radiation from Gliese 581 is Ie/Io = 10^(-0.4 * 4.2) = 48 times less than that of the Sun. Taking into account the Stefan-Boltzmann law and balance temperature, Re/Ro = (Ic/Io)^(1/2). According to the generalized Kepler's third law: Tc = Te * (Ro/Re)^(3/2) * (Me/Mo)^(-1/2) = 365 days * 48^(3/4) / 0.31^(1/2) ~ 36 days.

Критерии оценивания (Всего 10 пт):
- Conditions as on the Earth, the same temperature — 1 pt.
- Correct taking the necessary data from the tables — 0.5 pt.
- Finding (any way) that the radiation from Gliese 581 is about 48 times less than that of the Sun — 2.5 pt.
- Dependence on R — 1 pt.
- Correct using the generalized Kepler's third law, calculations — 2 pt.
- Final calculations and correct result — 1 pt.

parts.question: What is the apparent magnitude of our Sun when observed from the planet Gliese 581 g?
parts.reference:
The magnitude of the Sun, visible from any remote location is Mo = mp + 5 log (206265) - 5 lg p. The magnitude of the Sun as seen from the system of Gliese 581 is Mg = -26.74 + 26.57 - 5 log 0.16 = -0.17 - (-3.98) = 3.8.

Критерии оценивания (Всего 5 пт):
- Formulae for magnitude of the Sun (any way solution) — 3 pt.
- Correct calculations — 2 pt.

parts.question: What is the approximate constellation in which our Sun will be seen when observed from the planet Gliese 581 g?
parts.reference:
While observing from the planet Gliese 581 g, our Sun will be at a point opposite to where the system of Gliese 581 is seen from Earth. Because Gliese 581 is located in the zodiacal constellation of Libra, the sun will be approximately in the opposite zodiacal constellation, that is, in the constellation of Aries.

Критерии оценивания (Всего 3 пт):
- Understanding that Gliese 581 is located in the zodiacal constellation of Libra — 1 pt.
- Sun will be at opposite point — 1 pt.
- Answer: constellation of Aries — 1 pt.

tasks.title: XVIII century. Midday
tasks.statement: Dubingiai is the nearest town to the accommodation place of XVIII IAO. There were different systems of units of measurement in the history of science. This problem is to use historical (at present obsolete) units of measurement.

parts.question: Calculate the capacity of the solar energy that in the end of the XVIII century fell on the unit of area of the territory in the outskirts of Dubingiai at midday time: in winter, in spring, in autumn, and in summer. The answer must be given using only the «new» physical units, which were coming into operation in those days in this area: horse-powers per square verst.
parts.reference:
Solar constant in units of the end of the XVIII century: A_XVIII = 2.12 * 10^6 hp / vrst^2. Altitudes of the midday sun: in winter hw = 11.5°, in spring/autumn ho = 35.0°, in summer hs = 58.5°. Power flux W = A * sin h. Results: in winter Ww = 420 000 hp/vrst^2, in spring and autumn Wo = 1 220 000 hp/vrst^2, in summer Ws = 1 810 000 hp/vrst^2.

Критерии оценивания (Всего 5 пт включая common 2 pt):
- Calculation of the solar constant in necessary units, result 2.12*10^6 hp / vrst^2 — 2 pt.
- Latitudes the same as now (about 54.7° — 55.2°) — 1 pt.
- Calculation of altitudes of midday Sun in winter, spring, autumn, summer — 1 pt.
- W = A*sin h, correct final calculations — 1 pt.

parts.question: Estimate also the capacity of the solar energy incident on a local horse those times. The answer must also be expressed in physical units, which were coming into operation in those days. What can be surprising about the right answer?
parts.reference:
Cross-sectional area of a horse perpendicular to the sun-rays is 1-3 arsh^2. Solar constant in these units equals to 0.94 hp / arsh^2. Thus, a horse standing in the sun, receives about 1-3 horse-powers of solar radiation!

Критерии оценивания (Всего 3 пт):
- Correct understanding on what the answer may depend — 0.5 pt.
- Correct model of horse, including the picture — 0.5 pt.
- The cross-sectional area of a horse perpendicular to the sun-rays is 1-3 arsh^2 — 0.5 pt.
- Correct calculations and result about 1-3 hp — 1 pt.
- Common conclusion about surprise that horse standing in the sun, receives about one to three horse-powers of solar radiation — 0.5 pt.

tasks.title: XXI century. Midday
tasks.statement: As is known, the Republic of Lithuania uses zone with winter time UT+02 and summer time UT+03. Calculate and draw a conclusion about the following:

parts.question: Are there any places in Lithuania, where today (September 8, 2013) the Sun will be exactly in the south at a time when the watches of residents will show just 12:00? («да-yes» or «нет-no»).
parts.reference:
Today (on September 8) the summer time is in operation, watches ahead UT by 3 hours. Local mean solar time coincide with this time on the meridian 45° East, located too far to the east. Equation of time correction is not more than 4° in longitude. Answer: «нет-no».

Критерии оценивания (Всего 3 пт):
- Summer time, meridian 45°, far to the east, so not possible — 2 pt.
- Mention that adding of the equation of time — correction not more than 4° in longitude — 1 pt.

parts.question: And in general, on the other days of the year, are there such places? («да-yes» or «нет-no»). If 'yes', then calculate in what dates, if 'no', then justify it by calculations.
parts.reference:
During winter time operation, local mean solar time corresponds to meridian 30° East. Apparent solar noon is defined by equation of time. Apparent noon will occur at 12:00 of Lithuanian time somewhere at the territory of the country if values of n were below -15 minutes. This happens from October 18 to November 17. Answer: «да-yes», October 18 - November 17.

Критерии оценивания (Всего 5 пт):
- For any day during summer time the situation is similar to #5.1 — 1 pt.
- Finding longitudes of Lithuania, meridian 30° is not too far — 1 pt.
- Correct equation of time using — 1 pt.
- Values of n were below -15 minutes — 1 pt.
- Finding the period from October 18 to November 17 (approximately) — 1 pt.

tasks.title: Supernova remnant
tasks.statement: An X-ray image of supernova remnant (SNR) Cas A located at a distance of d = 3400 pc was obtained using Chandra Space Observatory. The negative of this image is shown in Fig. SNR. The boundaries of the SNR region are marked by a circle. The scale of the image is shown in the upper left corner of the figure. A dot located close to the center of the circle is the neutron star — the remaining core of the collapsed star. The rectangular marks outside the circle are given for the reference when determining the center of the circle. Assume that the amount of energy released in the supernova explosion was about E_SN = 10^46 J, 1% of which drives the expansion of the remnant. The average density of the matter in the SNR is rho = 10^(-17) kg/m^3.

parts.question: Estimate the age of the SNR Cas A.
parts.reference:
Angular radius theta = 170", linear radius R = 8.6 * 10^16 m. Mass M = 2.7 * 10^30 kg. Expansion velocity v = (2 * E_kin / M)^(1/2) = 8.6 * 10^5 m/s. Age t = 0.6 * R / v ~ 200 years (taking into account 1 significant digit).

Критерии оценивания (Всего 6 пт включая common 2 pt):
- Correct measurements of distances — 0.5 pt.
- Finding necessary distances and mass — 1.5 pt.
- Energy, finding typical speeds — 1 pt.
- Final the time, correct calculations — 1 pt.
- Most data was done very roughly, with maximum 1 significant digit, follow this principle — 2 pt.

parts.question: Calculate the average velocity of the motion of the neutron star from the center of the SNR.
parts.reference:
Angular distance of neutron star from center d = 10.5", linear distance s_NS = 5.3 * 10^13 km. Velocity u = s_NS / t ~ 10^3 km/s (~ 900 km/s).

Критерии оценивания (Всего 4 пт включая common 2 pt):
- Correct measurements of distance from the center — 0.5 pt.
- Calculations and correct answer — 1.5 pt.
- Most data was done very roughly, with maximum 1 significant digit, follow this principle — 2 pt.
